headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.8535). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an effect size of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.48–1.21), indicating no statistically significant association between tea and uterine cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 78.67%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
